selection.symbolic_inputs: three one-cell typed event-history ranges with arbitrary value kinds, values, and fixed-point ownership
selection.exhaustive_test_infeasible_because: the product of typed values, ownership masks, and invalid-input injection is not practically enumerable
selection.counterexample_means: event-history advancement can lose type fidelity or partially mutate pre values on rejection

assumptions: typed_value generates only lattice-valid values (Real from i16/4.0, Integer whole f64, Boolean 0/1, Enumeration >= 1), so the kernel's type-validity clauses are exercised only through the single injected invalid position
the invalid injection is a NaN placed in the last lane's current value, so rejection is proven for that representative invalid typed input rather than every invalid encoding
unwind bound 16 covers three one-cell ranges at the harness's fixed iteration shape; longer ranges, a wider range count, or a different iteration shape are outside the proof
advance_event_iteration_ranges is the production kernel; callers that bypass it or mutate EventIterationRange backing slices directly are outside the proof
the claim relies on the pinned Kani and Rust lowering and its f64 model; the numeric generators do not cover every finite f64 encoding or negative zero

bound.domain: three one-cell production event-history ranges with arbitrary value kinds, typed values, fixed-point ownership, and invalid-input injection
